paper.tldr: A taxonomy of scientists’ visions for AI is developed, observing that their appeal comes from promises to improve productivity and objectivity by overcoming human shortcomings.

paper.title: Artificial intelligence tools expand scientists’ impact but contract science’s focus
paper.tldr: An accelerated adoption of AI tools among scientists and consistent professional advantages associated with AI usage are shown, but a collective narrowing of scientific focus is shown, highlighting a tension between personal advancement and collective scientific progress.

paper.title: The simulation of judgment in LLMs
paper.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
paper.tldr: This work compares six LLMs to expert ratings and human evaluations under an identical, structured framework and suggests that they may rely on lexical associations and statistical priors rather than contextual reasoning or normative criteria.
